fruits.extendedStory: The woman driving the horses is not who she used to be. She started out as Eirene, goddess of peace, holding a laurel wreath. After her return, Schinkel gave her an oak wreath with the Prussian eagle, and she became Victoria, goddess of victory. Carl Gotthard Langhans designed the gate itself for King Frederick William II. It is named after the town of Brandenburg an der Havel.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Die Frau, die die Pferde lenkt, ist nicht mehr, wer sie einmal war. Sie begann als Eirene, Göttin des Friedens, mit einem Lorbeerkranz. Nach ihrer Rückkehr gab Schinkel ihr einen Eichenkranz mit dem preußischen Adler, und aus ihr wurde Victoria, die Göttin des Sieges. Das Tor selbst entwarf Carl Gotthard Langhans für König Friedrich Wilhelm II. Benannt ist es nach der Stadt Brandenburg an der Havel.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The woman driving the horses is not who she used to be. She started out as Eirene, goddess of peace, holding a laurel wreath. After her return, Schinkel gave her an oak wreath with the Prussian eagle, and she became Victoria, goddess of victory. Carl Gotthard Langhans designed the gate itself for King Frederick William II. It is named after the town of Brandenburg an der Havel.

localizedStory.de: Als die Quadriga aus Paris zurückkam, nannten die Berliner den wochenlangen Transport, so heißt es, die Retourkutsche.
localizedStory.en: The story goes that when the Quadriga came home from Paris, Berliners called the long trip the Retourkutsche, the coach sent back.

fruits.name: Brandenburger Tor
fruits.story: The story goes that when the Quadriga came home from Paris, Berliners called the long trip the Retourkutsche, the coach sent back.

fruits.extendedStory: Julius Carl Raschdorff designed it in the Renaissance Revival style, borrowing domes and columns from Italian churches centuries older. Building took eleven years and finished in 1905. Much of it later had to be rebuilt, and that work was finished in 1975. So the stone around you is not all the same age. Some of it is decades younger than the rest.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Julius Carl Raschdorff entwarf ihn im Stil der Neorenaissance, mit Kuppel und Säulen nach dem Vorbild viel älterer italienischer Kirchen. Der Bau dauerte elf Jahre und war 1905 fertig. Später musste vieles neu aufgebaut werden, und diese Arbeit endete erst 1975. Der Stein um dich ist also nicht überall gleich alt. Manches ist Jahrzehnte jünger als der Rest.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Julius Carl Raschdorff designed it in the Renaissance Revival style, borrowing domes and columns from Italian churches centuries older. Building took eleven years and finished in 1905. Much of it later had to be rebuilt, and that work was finished in 1975. So the stone around you is not all the same age. Some of it is decades younger than the rest.

localizedStory.de: Kaiser Wilhelm II. gab diesen Dom in Auftrag, und seine Kuppel ragt 98 Meter hoch.
localizedStory.en: Emperor Wilhelm II ordered this cathedral, and its dome rises 98 metres above the ground.

fruits.name: Berliner Dom
fruits.story: Emperor Wilhelm II ordered this cathedral, and its dome rises 98 metres above the ground.

fruits.extendedStory: The name makes sense once you know who built the tower. Deutsche Post, the post office of East Germany, ordered it, and Hermann Henselmann designed it. It opened in 1969 and reaches 368 metres. Nobody planned a cross on it. The sun puts one there anyway, on every clear day it shines straight at the ball.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Der Name ergibt Sinn, wenn man weiß, wer den Turm baute. Die Deutsche Post der DDR gab ihn in Auftrag, Hermann Henselmann entwarf ihn. 1969 wurde er eröffnet, und er ist 368 Meter hoch. Ein Kreuz hatte niemand eingeplant. Die Sonne malt es trotzdem hin, an jedem klaren Tag, an dem sie direkt auf die Kugel scheint.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The name makes sense once you know who built the tower. Deutsche Post, the post office of East Germany, ordered it, and Hermann Henselmann designed it. It opened in 1969 and reaches 368 metres. Nobody planned a cross on it. The sun puts one there anyway, on every clear day it shines straight at the ball.

localizedStory.de: Scheint die Sonne direkt auf die Kugel, erscheint dort ein Lichtkreuz. Sein Spitzname: die Rache des Papstes.
localizedStory.en: When the sun hits the steel ball, look for a cross of light. It is known as the Pope's revenge.

fruits.name: Berliner Fernsehturm
fruits.story: When the sun hits the steel ball, look for a cross of light. It is known as the Pope's revenge.

fruits.extendedStory: The city built it for itself, not for a prince. Hermann Friedrich Waesemann gave it round arches and rows of windows in the Renaissance Revival style, borrowing the look of Italian palaces. Its tower rises 74 metres over the square. Here citizens, not a royal court, decided how grand a town hall should look. So Berlin's council went to work in a palace of its own.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Die Stadt baute es für sich selbst, nicht für einen Fürsten. Hermann Friedrich Waesemann gab ihm Rundbögen und Fensterreihen im Stil der Neorenaissance, nach dem Vorbild italienischer Paläste. Sein Turm ragt 74 Meter über den Platz. Hier entschieden Bürger und kein Hof, wie prächtig ein Rathaus aussehen darf. So zog Berlins Stadtregierung in einen eigenen Palast.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The city built it for itself, not for a prince. Hermann Friedrich Waesemann gave it round arches and rows of windows in the Renaissance Revival style, borrowing the look of Italian palaces. Its tower rises 74 metres over the square. Here citizens, not a royal court, decided how grand a town hall should look. So Berlin's council went to work in a palace of its own.

localizedStory.de: Eigentlich heißt es Berliner Rathaus. Den Spitznamen Rotes Rathaus verdankt es seiner Ziegelfassade.
localizedStory.en: Its proper name is the Berliner Rathaus. It is known as the Rotes Rathaus, after the colour of the bricks on its front.

fruits.name: Rotes Rathaus
fruits.story: Its proper name is the Berliner Rathaus. It is known as the Rotes Rathaus, after the colour of the bricks on its front.

fruits.extendedStory: In 1990 the treasures turned up again. A Berliner brought them to the Märkisches Museum as part of an inheritance. When they were checked, 31 coins, one engraving and Elector Frederick III's red velvet purse were missing. The church itself once stood in ruins. Rebuilt, it is a museum today, and Berlin's newly elected city parliament once met here too.

localizedExtendedStory.de: 1990 tauchten die Schätze wieder auf. Ein Berliner brachte sie als Teil seiner Erbschaft ins Märkische Museum. Beim Prüfen fehlten 31 Münzen, ein Kupferstich und der rote Samtbeutel von Kurfürst Friedrich III. Die Kirche selbst lag einst in Trümmern. Wiederaufgebaut ist sie heute ein Museum, und auch das neu gewählte Abgeordnetenhaus für die ganze Stadt tagte hier.
localizedExtendedStory.en: In 1990 the treasures turned up again. A Berliner brought them to the Märkisches Museum as part of an inheritance. When they were checked, 31 coins, one engraving and Elector Frederick III's red velvet purse were missing. The church itself once stood in ruins. Rebuilt, it is a museum today, and Berlin's newly elected city parliament once met here too.

localizedStory.de: Jahrhundertelang kamen bei jeder Reparatur des Turms Münzen und handgeschriebene Chroniken in die Turmkugeln.
localizedStory.en: For centuries, whenever the tower was repaired, coins and handwritten chronicles were sealed into its tower balls.

fruits.name: Nikolaikirche
fruits.story: For centuries, whenever the tower was repaired, coins and handwritten chronicles were sealed into its tower balls.

fruits.extendedStory: Those facades nearly vanished. In 1950 they were to be knocked off, and the tenants who lived here stopped it. Kurt Berndt built eight courtyards in all, mixing workshops with homes. The name goes back further, to Berlin's town commander von Hacke. He had the marshy ground around the market drained, and the market and later the courtyards took his name.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Diese Fassaden wären fast verschwunden. 1950 sollten sie abgeschlagen werden, und die Mieter, die hier wohnten, verhinderten es. Kurt Berndt baute insgesamt acht Höfe, mit Werkstätten und Wohnungen unter einem Dach. Der Name reicht weiter zurück, zu Berlins Stadtkommandant von Hacke. Er ließ das sumpfige Gelände um den Markt trockenlegen, und Markt und später die Höfe tragen seinen Namen.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Those facades nearly vanished. In 1950 they were to be knocked off, and the tenants who lived here stopped it. Kurt Berndt built eight courtyards in all, mixing workshops with homes. The name goes back further, to Berlin's town commander von Hacke. He had the marshy ground around the market drained, and the market and later the courtyards took his name.

localizedStory.de: Zähl die Fenster in Hof I. August Endell gab ihnen 41 verschiedene Formen, dazu einen geschwungenen Dachfirst und farbige Verblendsteine.
localizedStory.en: Count the windows in Courtyard One. August Endell gave them 41 shapes, around a curving roof ridge and coloured bricks.

fruits.name: Hackesche Höfe
fruits.story: Count the windows in Courtyard One. August Endell gave them 41 shapes, around a curving roof ridge and coloured bricks.

fruits.extendedStory: Neoclassical builders copied the calm columns and plain triangles of ancient Greece. The king wanted a guard house, and Schinkel answered in that style. Work began and ended within 1818, quick going for cut stone. A guard house hardly needed temple columns. Schinkel gave it them anyway, and that grand touch on a modest job is what makes the building worth a look.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Klassizistische Baumeister ahmten die ruhigen Säulen und schlichten Dreiecksgiebel des alten Griechenland nach. Der König wollte eine Wache, und Schinkel antwortete in diesem Stil. Bau und Fertigstellung fielen beide in das Jahr 1818, schnell für behauenen Stein. Eine Wache brauchte eigentlich keine Tempelsäulen. Schinkel gab ihr trotzdem welche, und dieser große Auftritt für eine bescheidene Aufgabe macht den Bau sehenswert.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Neoclassical builders copied the calm columns and plain triangles of ancient Greece. The king wanted a guard house, and Schinkel answered in that style. Work began and ended within 1818, quick going for cut stone. A guard house hardly needed temple columns. Schinkel gave it them anyway, and that grand touch on a modest job is what makes the building worth a look.

localizedStory.de: Karl Friedrich Schinkel gab einer schlichten Wache das Gesicht eines griechischen Tempels, für König Friedrich Wilhelm III.
localizedStory.en: Karl Friedrich Schinkel gave a humble guard house the face of a Greek temple, for King Frederick William III.

fruits.name: Neue Wache
fruits.story: Karl Friedrich Schinkel gave a humble guard house the face of a Greek temple, for King Frederick William III.

fruits.extendedStory: Even so, the altar in the central hall was rebuilt just in part. To this day nobody knows why its builders chose not to rebuild it completely. Alfred Messel designed the museum, in a Neoclassical style that borrows its columns from ancient temples. It carries the name of Pergamon. Walking past, you pass a puzzle that has stayed unsolved for more than a century.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Trotzdem wurde der Altar im zentralen Saal nur teilweise wieder aufgebaut. Warum man darauf verzichtete, ihn ganz zu rekonstruieren, ist bis heute unklar. Alfred Messel entwarf das Museum im klassizistischen Stil, mit Säulen nach dem Vorbild antiker Tempel. Es trägt den Namen von Pergamon. Wer hier vorbeigeht, geht an einem Rätsel vorbei, das seit über einem Jahrhundert ungelöst ist.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Even so, the altar in the central hall was rebuilt just in part. To this day nobody knows why its builders chose not to rebuild it completely. Alfred Messel designed the museum, in a Neoclassical style that borrows its columns from ancient temples. It carries the name of Pergamon. Walking past, you pass a puzzle that has stayed unsolved for more than a century.

localizedStory.de: Italienische Restauratoren setzten den Fries des Altars hier aus tausenden Bruchstücken wieder zusammen. Damit man ihn zusammenhängend zeigen konnte, entstand eigens ein Museum.
localizedStory.en: Italian restorers pieced the altar's frieze back together here from thousands of fragments. A museum was built just to show it in one run.

fruits.name: Pergamonmuseum
fruits.story: Italian restorers pieced the altar's frieze back together here from thousands of fragments. A museum was built just to show it in one run.

fruits.extendedStory: Frederick II wanted the square to look grand. He had the architect Karl von Gontard add two domed towers beside its two churches. They were there to be looked at. The square's own name comes from soldiers: the Gens d'armes, a regiment of armoured horsemen once quartered here. Look for Schiller's statue too. It was cleared away for the Olympic Games of 1936, and came back in 1989.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Friedrich II. wollte dem Platz Wirkung geben und ließ den Architekten Karl von Gontard zwei Kuppeltürme neben die beiden Kirchen setzen. Sie waren zum Anschauen da. Der Name des Platzes kommt von Soldaten: den Gens d'armes, einem Regiment schwerer Reiter, das einst hier untergebracht war. Such auch Schillers Denkmal. Zur Olympiade 1936 wurde es entfernt und erst 1989 wieder aufgestellt.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Frederick II wanted the square to look grand. He had the architect Karl von Gontard add two domed towers beside its two churches. They were there to be looked at. The square's own name comes from soldiers: the Gens d'armes, a regiment of armoured horsemen once quartered here. Look for Schiller's statue too. It was cleared away for the Olympic Games of 1936, and came back in 1989.

localizedStory.de: Der Französische Dom ist keine Bischofskirche. Dom kommt hier vom französischen dôme, Kuppel, und der Turm hat gar keine geistliche Aufgabe.
localizedStory.en: No cathedral stands here. Dom in Französischer Dom is the French dôme, a cupola, and the tower has no church job at all.

fruits.name: Gendarmenmarkt
fruits.story: No cathedral stands here. Dom in Französischer Dom is the French dôme, a cupola, and the tower has no church job at all.

fruits.extendedStory: After 1750 the Hausvogtei, a court of appeal, moved here, and the square took its name. Before that it had been Schinkenplatz, ham square. Later the streets around it grew into a world-famous garment district. At the U-Bahn exit stand three tall mirrors, like the ones in a fitting room. Nearby, 19 steps carry the names and house numbers of its fashion houses.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Die Hausvogtei war das Hofgericht, das nach 1750 hierher zog, und der Platz übernahm ihren Namen. Vorher hieß er Schinkenplatz. Später wurde die Gegend ein weltbekanntes Konfektionsviertel, also ein Zentrum der Kleidermacher. Am Ausgang der U-Bahn stehen drei hohe Spiegel wie in einer Umkleide, und 19 Stufen tragen die Namen und Hausnummern der Modefirmen.
localizedExtendedStory.en: After 1750 the Hausvogtei, a court of appeal, moved here, and the square took its name. Before that it had been Schinkenplatz, ham square. Later the streets around it grew into a world-famous garment district. At the U-Bahn exit stand three tall mirrors, like the ones in a fitting room. Nearby, 19 steps carry the names and house numbers of its fashion houses.

localizedStory.de: Eine alte Redewendung warnte, so heißt es: Wer die Wahrheit weiß und saget sie frei, der kommt in Berlin in die Hausvogtei.
localizedStory.en: Old Berlin folklore warned: tell the truth freely, and you end up in the Hausvogtei. That was the court prison right here.

fruits.name: Hausvogteiplatz
fruits.story: Old Berlin folklore warned: tell the truth freely, and you end up in the Hausvogtei. That was the court prison right here.

fruits.extendedStory: Beneath your feet, the roadway is sheet metal under a thin coat of asphalt. Before it came, there was no bridge here at all for 47 years. The crossing honours a builder called Ebert, not President Friedrich Ebert. He set up a private bridge company in 1819 and charged tolls. An earlier bridge wore boar heads on its lamp bases, a joke on Ebert, since Eber means boar.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Die Fahrbahn besteht aus Blechplatten mit einer dünnen Schicht Asphalt. Vorher gab es hier 47 Jahre lang gar keine Brücke. Benannt ist sie nach einem Erbauer namens Ebert, nicht nach Reichspräsident Friedrich Ebert. Der Berliner Hauseigentümer gründete 1819 eine private Brückengesellschaft und nahm Maut. Eine frühere Brücke trug Eberköpfe an den Leuchtensockeln, ein Scherz auf seinen Namen.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Beneath your feet, the roadway is sheet metal under a thin coat of asphalt. Before it came, there was no bridge here at all for 47 years. The crossing honours a builder called Ebert, not President Friedrich Ebert. He set up a private bridge company in 1819 and charged tolls. An earlier bridge wore boar heads on its lamp bases, a joke on Ebert, since Eber means boar.

localizedStory.de: Diese Brücke war ein Provisorium für zwei Jahre, gebaut aus Teilen abgebauter Stahlhochstraßen. Abgebaut wurde sie danach nie.
localizedStory.en: This bridge was a stopgap meant for two years. It is built from parts of old elevated steel roads, and nobody took it away.

fruits.name: Ebertsbrücke
fruits.story: This bridge was a stopgap meant for two years. It is built from parts of old elevated steel roads, and nobody took it away.

fruits.extendedStory: They were found in abandoned barracks around Berlin, and the museum took them in. Metal rods, bits of plastic, laths and cable went into them too. The museum is the archive of the Deutscher Werkbund, a group founded in Munich in 1907 by twelve artists and twelve firms. It is new to this street. After losing its old home in Kreuzberg, it reopened here in 2024.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Gefunden wurden sie in verlassenen Kasernen rund um Berlin, und das Museum nahm sie in seine Sammlung auf. Auch Metallstangen, Plastikstücke, Latten und Kabel stecken darin. Das Museum ist das Archiv des Deutschen Werkbunds, 1907 in München von zwölf Künstlern und zwölf Firmen gegründet. In dieser Straße ist es neu. Nach der Kündigung in Kreuzberg öffnete es 2024 hier wieder.
localizedExtendedStory.en: They were found in abandoned barracks around Berlin, and the museum took them in. Metal rods, bits of plastic, laths and cable went into them too. The museum is the archive of the Deutscher Werkbund, a group founded in Munich in 1907 by twelve artists and twelve firms. It is new to this street. After losing its old home in Kreuzberg, it reopened here in 2024.

localizedStory.de: In der Sammlung stehen Antennen, die russische Soldaten aus Blechresten, Draht und Schnur bauten. Sie wirken fast wie Totempfähle.
localizedStory.en: Its collection holds TV antennas Soviet soldiers built from scrap metal, wire and string. They look almost like totem poles.

fruits.name: Werkbundarchiv - Museum der Dinge
fruits.story: Its collection holds TV antennas Soviet soldiers built from scrap metal, wire and string. They look almost like totem poles.

fruits.extendedStory: Emperor Wilhelm II ordered the new home, and Ernst von Ihne designed it. Work began in 1903. Ihne chose the baroque revival style, heavy with curves, columns and carved ornament, and the library looks like a palace. The building stands 28 metres tall. Behind it, books gathered since the seventeenth century finally had a grand house of their own.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Kaiser Wilhelm II. gab das neue Haus in Auftrag, Ernst von Ihne entwarf es. Der Bau begann 1903. Ihne wählte den Neobarock, voller Schwünge, Säulen und Schmuck, und so wirkt die Bibliothek wie ein Palast. Das Gebäude ist 28 Meter hoch. Hinter seinen Mauern bekamen Bücher, gesammelt seit dem siebzehnten Jahrhundert, endlich ein prächtiges eigenes Zuhause.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Emperor Wilhelm II ordered the new home, and Ernst von Ihne designed it. Work began in 1903. Ihne chose the baroque revival style, heavy with curves, columns and carved ornament, and the library looks like a palace. The building stands 28 metres tall. Behind it, books gathered since the seventeenth century finally had a grand house of their own.

localizedStory.de: Diese Bibliothek ist viel älter als ihr Haus. Sie entstand 1661 und wartete über zweieinhalb Jahrhunderte auf dieses Gebäude.
localizedStory.en: This library is far older than its house. It began in 1661 and waited over two and a half centuries for this building.

fruits.name: Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin
fruits.story: This library is far older than its house. It began in 1661 and waited over two and a half centuries for this building.

fruits.extendedStory: In 1937 it had to hand over its own house here, to make room for the state's chief building inspector. That old house was destroyed in the last days of the war. The academy itself goes back much further. Frederick III, an elector, founded it in 1696 as an academy of painting, sculpture and building. Werner Durth worked with Behnisch on the new house.

localizedExtendedStory.de: 1937 musste sie ihr eigenes Haus hier räumen, um Platz für den obersten Bauinspektor des Staates zu machen. Das alte Haus wurde in den letzten Kriegstagen zerstört. Die Akademie selbst reicht viel weiter zurück. Kurfürst Friedrich III. gründete sie 1696 als Akademie der Mahl-, Bild- und Baukunst. Werner Durth arbeitete mit Behnisch am neuen Haus.
localizedExtendedStory.en: In 1937 it had to hand over its own house here, to make room for the state's chief building inspector. That old house was destroyed in the last days of the war. The academy itself goes back much further. Frederick III, an elector, founded it in 1696 as an academy of painting, sculpture and building. Werner Durth worked with Behnisch on the new house.

localizedStory.de: Nach fast siebzig Jahren kehrte die Akademie an ihre alte Adresse zurück, in einen Glasbau von Günter Behnisch.
localizedStory.en: After nearly seventy years away, the academy came back to its old address, into a glass building by Günter Behnisch.

fruits.name: Akademie der Künste
fruits.story: After nearly seventy years away, the academy came back to its old address, into a glass building by Günter Behnisch.
